headline: Learned models link peptide-MHC binding and variant-driven drug effects
label: Genetic Variant Drug Prediction
summary: PepCL, BoltzOmics and a Mendelian randomization atlas each extend predictive models to new assay, structural or population-genetic data.
synthesis: The shared thread is computational prediction of how molecular and genetic variation shapes drug- and peptide-level outcomes, using learned or structure-based models applied to new data. PepCL applies replay-based continual learning to update peptide-MHC class I predictors with new assay data while preserving prior knowledge. BoltzOmics uses Boltz-2 structure prediction to estimate how genetic variants alter drug binding affinity, validated on hERG. The third item differs in method: genetics-led Mendelian randomization across UK Biobank, FinnGen and MVP anticipates drug adverse reactions and is released as an interactive atlas and web tool. What is new is the shift from static predictors toward incrementally updated models, structural variant-effect estimation, and population genetic evidence linked to drug safety.
